page: Amazon Web Services m5d.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by dual Intel Xeon 8175M processors. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For local storage, the server is equipped with 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and it supports a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m5d.metal demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core score of 82016.64 and a Passmark CPU score of 56893.67. Memory performance is also strong, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 216.75 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 92.26 GB/sec. The server excels in database and web-serving operations, achieving 76.56 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 48.67 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance remains average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1209.0, and LLM text generation speeds are poor, dropping to 5.11 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates hypervisor overhead, allowing direct access to physical resources and the 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. This high resource density makes it a viable option for workloads requiring direct hardware access without the virtualization layer. The server is well-suited for large-scale databases, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded enterprise applications, though it is less optimal for workloads heavily reliant on single-threaded performance or GPU acceleration.
